problem: The vector $v=⟨-6,4⟩$ is rotated ${30}^{∘}$ counterclockwise about the origin. Find the image of $v$ under this rotation.

feedback.problem:
The vector $v=⟨-\sqrt{2},\,\,2\sqrt{3}⟩$ is rotated $\frac{5\pi }{4}$ radians **clockwise** about the origin. Find the image of $v$ under this rotation.

${v}^{′}=⟨$ 
{{field-1}}, 
{{field-2}}
$⟩$
feedback.worked_solution:
A rotation of $\frac{5\pi }{4}$ radians *clockwise* about the origin is represented by the matrix 

$$
{R}_{(-5\pi /4)}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{5\pi }{4}) & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{5\pi }{4}) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{5\pi }{4}) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{5\pi }{4})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image ${v}^{′}$ under the action of the matrix ${R}_{(-5\pi /4)}$, we compute the matrix product, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}^{′} & ={R}_{(-5\pi /4)}\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{2} \\ 2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-\sqrt{6} \\ -1-\sqrt{6}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the image is ${v}^{′}=⟨1-\sqrt{6},-1-\sqrt{6}⟩.$
